doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: June Tyson, the only woman in the band
summary: Allen says June Tyson was respected like a sister, so her being the only woman caused no problems.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did it change the dynamic of the band when June Tyson became part of the group? And do you think it was difficult for her being the only woman in the group?

No because she was the kind of woman that could be with me and it wasn’t about those sexy things and all that B.S. you know. It was nothing. Because she carried herself in that manner that you know she was more like in the family, like a sister you know. And that’s the way she carried herself. So she was the only woman in the band with all these men, you know, but everybody had mutual respect for her.
